description: A one-block data table (Table 1, "Mechanical properties of studied steels") rendered as an image, with six columns and three data rows; no figure panels, axes, scale bars or images are present. Columns are headed, exactly as printed: "Steel", "Grian size/ μm" (sic, typo for grain size), "YS/MPa", "UTS/MPa", "EI/%" and "Impact energy/ J", with a horizontal rule under the header. Row 1 (S1000): 3.17 μm, 955 ± 7 MPa, 1126 ± 3 MPa, 55.5 ± 1.3 %, 29.2 ± 2.0 J. Row 2 (S1050): 3.84 μm, 945 ± 14 MPa, 1113 ± 3 MPa, 55.8 ± 0.4 %, 42.8 ± 0.4 J. Row 3 (MHT): 7.31 μm, 910 ± 7 MPa, 1076 ± 2 MPa, 50.9 ± 3.0 %, 55.1 ± 2.2 J. All strength, elongation and impact values carry ± uncertainties. The table demonstrates the central trade-off claimed by the paper: as the grain size grows from 3.17 to 3.84 to 7.31 μm across S1000, S1050 and MHT, yield strength and ultimate tensile strength fall monotonically while impact energy rises monotonically, so the multi-stage heat-treated condition (MHT) reaches the highest toughness (55.1 J) at only a modest strength loss.

subfigures.description: Single tabular panel with header row (Steel; Grian size/μm; YS/MPa; UTS/MPa; EI/%; Impact energy/J) and three data rows for S1000, S1050 and MHT, all property values given with ± uncertainty.

observations.observation: The table is headed by six columns printed as 'Steel', 'Grian size/ μm', 'YS/MPa', 'UTS/MPa', 'EI/%' and 'Impact energy/ J', with three data rows labelled S1000, S1050 and MHT.
S1000 row values: grain size 3.17 μm, YS 955 ± 7 MPa, UTS 1126 ± 3 MPa, EI 55.5 ± 1.3 %, impact energy 29.2 ± 2.0 J.
S1050 row values: grain size 3.84 μm, YS 945 ± 14 MPa, UTS 1113 ± 3 MPa, EI 55.8 ± 0.4 %, impact energy 42.8 ± 0.4 J.
MHT row values: grain size 7.31 μm, YS 910 ± 7 MPa, UTS 1076 ± 2 MPa, EI 50.9 ± 3.0 %, impact energy 55.1 ± 2.2 J.
Across the three rows the grain size increases (3.17 → 3.84 → 7.31 μm) while YS and UTS decrease monotonically, and impact energy increases monotonically (29.2 → 42.8 → 55.1 J).
Elongation values are nearly identical for S1000 (55.5 %) and S1050 (55.8 %) and slightly lower for MHT (50.9 %), so the large grain-size increase of MHT costs little ductility.
The caption labels the table 'Table 1 Mechanical properties of studied steels' and spells the second column 'Grian size/μm'.
The citing text states YS and UTS decrease with increasing d_eff, with d_eff rising from 3.17 μm in S1000 to 3.84 μm in S1050 and the YS/UTS dropping by 10 MPa over that step.
The citing text states that MHT (d_eff 7.31 μm) has slightly lower YS, UTS and TEL than S1050, declining by 35, 37 and 4.6 %, respectively, at 25 °C.
The citing text reports S1000 with the lowest impact energy (29.2 J), S1050 with 42.8 J and MHT with the largest (55.1 J), an increase of 88.6 %.
The citing text calls the ductility measure 'TEL' while the table column is printed 'EI/%'; both refer to the same elongation values reported for the three specimens.
